text.p: Finning Ltd, the world's biggest dealer of Caterpillar Inc equipment, said Monday it expects "continued improvement" in 1997 earnings.

Strength should stem from modest increases in demand from Canada and Europe and strong growth in Chile, the company said. Finning earlier reported fourth quarter earnings rose to C$0.52 a share from C$0.44 a year earlier.

Investment analysts expect 1997 earnings in the range of C$2.25 to C$2.40 a share, Finning said. A company spokesman declined to comment on specific forecasts but said Finning was comfortable with that range.
1996 earnings were C$2.26 a share including a non-recurring gain of C$0.19 from property sales. It was the company's third consecutive year of record earnings.

Finning attributed the fourth quarter rise to strong sales of used equipment in Canada and brisk new equipment sales in Chile. Foreign sales accounted for 51 percent of Finning's revenues in 1996, up from 47 percent in 1995.
Fourth quarter revenues rose 17 percent in Chile, 11 percent in Canada and 6.7 percent in Britain.
Finning said talks were continuing with Unilever Plc to buy its H Leverton Ltd unit, which holds the Caterpillar franchise for parts of England not handled by Finning.

The talks are covered by a confidentality agreement and Finning said it could not release further details. Finning previously said it hoped to close the acquisition in the first quarter. Analysts have projected the acquisition would add about C$0.50 a share to Finning annual earnings initially, so a delay could prompt some to trim 1997 estimates.
